questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Vienna as my destination primarily for two reasons: that the University of Vienna is high-quality university, and that I have previously really enjoyed the city of Vienna.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find all necessary information. The Erasmus-Incoming team at the University of Vienna is very communicative, and they send all the information you need by email and refer to pages on their websites. The available information was very detailed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were frequent orientations, making it easy to attend one shortly after arrival. Other than this orientation I did not need any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find off-campus housing. The University of Vienna recommends using Housing Anywhere to find housing, and that is what I did. I had no issues.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really liked living off-campus. It enabled me to choose housing depending on what was most important to me, such as space, distance to university, neighborhood etc. It did not have any impact on my participation in social activities - there are many options through the Erasmus Student Network at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can't really make a judgement about on-campus housing, but I didn't hear anyone having issues with finding housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is very simple. At PolSci, you can apply for as many courses as you want and prioritize them based on your preference. You then get assigned all courses where you get a spot. The only challenging part was that the registration process takes place close to semester start which meant that I needed to ask UCPH if they could speed up the pre-approval process (which they were able to do).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can reach out to the Erasmus-Incoming team as well as coordinators and professors, but I did not find it necessary to do so.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied for twice as many courses as I needed just in case and got into all but one. You can deregister from courses until 2-3 weeks into the semester, meaning that you get to try out different courses if you're uncertain about which you want to take. This was a really nice option.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask UCPH if they can give you a quicker pre-approval if it usually takes a long time, so you can have peace of mind about the pre-approval. And if you get waitlisted for a course you really want, stay on the waitlist - many students deregister for courses in the first couple of weeks, so you may get a spot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose more demanding courses (according to the permanent Uni Vie students) due to interest and found the coursed to be a bit easier than UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more portfolio-style with several deliverables during the semester (you can also choose courses that only have one final sit-in exam, but these give less ECTS-points). The classes are also more classroom discussion than teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
210122-1 SE M11: EU Policy-Making for the Digital Age (12 ECTS)
210111-1 SE M7: Democratic Resilience: How Democracies Survive (9 ECTS)
210112-1 SE M7: Technology, Power, and Governance: Comparative Perspectives (9 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the research-practice seminar (M11). It was more work but also more practical which was fun to try. Otherwise, I specifically found the course on democratic resilience interesting because of the subject.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities through the Erasmus Student Network at the University of Vienna. They host sports events, dinners, bar events, museum visits, excursion etc. There's something for everyone. Just make sure to be quick to sign up for events, since spots are limited.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the dinners, bar meet-ups, museum visits and excursions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the opportunity to travel by train to nearby cities. There are many nice places in Austria, e.g. Melk, Hallstatt, Salzburg. Outside of Vienna it is super easy to take weekendtrips to Prague and Budapest - I really recommend that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take some courses that include group work

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The café-scene in Vienna and how beautiful the city is

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to use your time off to visit other places. Train travel from Vienna is really easy and cheap (especially if you buy your tickets a couple of weeks or more in advance).
Remember to look at the how the examination will work in the courses you are thinking about applying for. It can differ a lot.
Enjoy your time in one of the best cities in the world!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal growth from going somewhere new and not knowing what to expect - and having a great time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving back and forth, and having overlapping semesters because of the difference in semester structure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
